title: WildHandBench: A Benchmark for Handwritten Text Understanding that Challenges MLLMs and Humans
abstract: arXiv:2608.22959v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: While the top model on OmniDocBench now reaches 96.34% overall on printed-document parsing, the ability of current models to handle challenging handwritten documents remains largely uncharacterized. Existing benchmarks focus on isolated text or formulas, overlook handwritten tables and real-world degradation, and report aggregate accuracy without explaining why models fail.   We present WildHandBench, a benchmark containing 500 handwritten documents across three structures (free text, tables, formulas), four languages, and nine real-world scenarios. We introduce a Prior-Driven Error (PDE) metric that quantifies whether errors originate from language priors rather than visual evidence. translated_title: WildHandBench：一个挑战多模态大语言模型与人类的手写文本理解基准
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.22959v1 公告类型：交叉 摘要：尽管OmniDocBench上的顶尖模型在印刷文档解析方面整体准确率已达96.34%，但当前模型处理具有挑战性的手写文档的能力在很大程度上仍未被充分表征。现有基准侧重于孤立文本或公式，忽视了手写表格和现实世界的退化问题，并且仅报告聚合准确率而不解释模型失败的原因。我们提出了WildHandBench，一个包含500份手写文档的基准，涵盖三种结构（自由文本、表格、公式）、四种语言和九个现实世界场景。我们引入了一种先验驱动误差（PDE）指标，用于量化错误是否源于语言先验而非视觉证据。评估了18个最先进模型以及校准后的人类基线，我们发现：（1）最佳模型整体准确率仅为71.85%；（2）人类在所有模型上表现更优，但差距较小（77.09%对比71.85%）；（3）模型错误在定性上存在差异。
tldr: 该基准首次系统评估了多模态大语言模型在复杂手写文档上的表现，并引入先验驱动误差指标揭示模型失败源于语言先验而非视觉证据，且人类优势微弱。
en_tdlr: This benchmark systematically evaluates MLLMs on complex handwritten documents for the first time, introducing a prior-driven error metric to reveal that model failures stem from language priors rather than visual evidence, with humans showing only a narrow advantage.
